Focus:
- graphs
- DP
- patterns
- problem intuition
- consistency

Not trying to become a CP machine.
Just genuinely strong enough.

---

### systems thinking

Things I naturally keep learning:
- psychology
- emotional design
- human behavior
- communication
- storytelling
- aesthetics
- product systems
- interaction design

These matter heavily for the kind of builder I wanna become.

---

## things I eventually wanna explore

Future interests:
- emotional AI
- AI + holograms
- memory systems
- human-computer interaction
- adaptive interfaces
- AI companions
- safety systems
- intelligent environments
- creative AI systems

Basically:
technology that emotionally interacts with humans in meaningful ways.

---

## learning philosophy

I don’t wanna become someone who:
- memorizes buzzwords
- copies tutorials endlessly
- sounds smart online but can’t build

I wanna:
- deeply understand concepts
- create original systems
- think independently
- combine creativity with engineering
- build emotionally meaningful things

---

## current learning style

Best learning flow for me:
1. curiosity
2. project idea
3. confusion
4. experimentation
5. deeper questions
6. practical building
7. theory after context

That cycle works insanely well for my brain.

---

## long term vision

Eventually I wanna become someone who can naturally combine:
- AI
- engineering
- design
- storytelling
- emotional intelligence
- product thinking
- systems architecture

into one coherent identity.

Not just:
> “software engineer.”

Something much broader than that.

---

## reminder to future me

A lot of my writing sounds romantic on the surface,
but honestly most of it is about:
> wanting permanence in a world where everything keeps leaving.

---

At some point I started becoming more ambitious too.

Not just emotionally deep.
Restless.

I wanted:
- skills
- freedom
- impact
- meaningful work
- beautiful futures
- multidimensionality

I became obsessed with becoming capable.

Frontend.
Design.
Storytelling.
Communities.
AI.
Product thinking.
Teaching.
Building.

I didn’t want to become one thing.
I wanted to become someone who could create entire worlds from ideas.

---

Then came the phase where technology stopped feeling purely technical to me.

I started seeing:
- emotional systems
- human psychology in products
- loneliness in modern tech
- the way apps shape emotions
- how AI might emotionally affect humans

That’s where ideas like Casper started mattering deeply to me.

Not because:
> “AI companion cool.”

But because I genuinely wanted technology to feel softer.
Safer.
More human.

I wanted to build systems that understand emotions instead of exploiting them.

---

At the same time,
my personal life kept shaping me heavily.

Attachment.
Distance.
Ghosting.
People leaving.
People staying.
Late night conversations.
The fear of becoming replaceable.
The fear of caring too much.

A lot of my emotional growth happened through relationships that probably looked ordinary from outside but changed me internally forever.

I think some people permanently alter your emotional climate.

Even after they leave.

---

---

### Multi-Domain Thinking

- human behavior

---

## Long-Term Vision
